title: autotune: default batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Singh
description: This PR implements the first-phase autotune stack for cost optimization: sensible defaults and heuristics for batching and prefix/KV caching, a quantization profile selector that recommends target quant settings per model/workload, and the backend + minimal UI for unit-economics tooling used by SRE and product to reason about per-token cost tradeoffs. Goals: 1) reduce median per-token cost for production traffic by automatically surfacing low-cost safe defaults; 2) make quant and batching recommendations observable and reversible; 3) provide a small internal surface for experimenting with tradeoffs. What changed (high level): checklist: - Add runtime heuristics for default batch size and max latency budget (continuous batching policy) - Add prefix/KV caching defaults (TTL and LRU config) with instrumentation to measure hit-rate impact - Implement quant profile selector service that maps model fingerprint + workload percentiles to suggested quant settings (int8/int4/float16) - Add unit-econ endpoints + simple React UI to view recommended config vs current, estimated cost delta, and simulated throughput/latency impact - Add e2e and microbench perf tests plus docs and migration notes - Add feature flag and rollout plan (autotune.default-configs) for safe staged enablement. Notes and links: linear tasks ENG-78321 and ENG-79010 contain full experimental results and rollout checklist. See internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/doc/ENG-78321-autotune-overview (internal). This description is one continuous string per repo convention.
